touches.text: Once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus: the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py, the other code sites and the 82 proofs that run a sieve over themselves. No published client tool, no fifth exception. Akien 2026-11-13, on Q#88: "over the bus. that's what it's for?"
The exceptions are client tools a device publishes:

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. Akien 2026-11-09 (Q#77): "wouldn't it be easier (for the python code anyway) to see if the imports do not include other device paths?"

conflicts.why: 9.4.3.3.4 states: 'Once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus... No published client tool, no fifth exception.' The outline forbids the published-tool approach the ticket proposes. The four existing published exceptions (Database 2.3.7.1.1, Librarian 2.3.7.1.2, Trouble 2.3.7.1.3, Scratch bus 2.3.7.1.4) are the allowed set. Adding inspect_wire as a fifth violates this explicit constraint.
